research_text:
## Research brief

### 1. API and reported event

`javax.crypto.Cipher` is the JCE API for encryption and decryption; it also supports key wrapping and unwrapping. `getInstance` selects a transformation, and `init` selects the operation mode and supplies a key or certificate and, where applicable, parameters and randomness. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))

The reported finding concerns a **method-call sequence**, not a particular cipher text or constant: an `init` event occurs after a modeled operation has completed. The supplied CrySL rule places `Init+` before its modeled operation events and does not include a subsequent `Init` in its `ORDER` expression. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

That restriction is **not the general JCA contract**. Oracle documents reinitialization as discarding the cipher’s previously acquired state. For GCM encryption, Oracle expressly recommends reinitializing with a different IV after each encryption when the same key is used. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))

### 2. Documented usage and remediation guidance

- **Transformation and initialization:** A transformation may specify `algorithm/mode/padding`; an algorithm-only name leaves mode and padding to provider defaults. Initialize for the intended encrypt, decrypt, wrap, or unwrap operation with appropriate key material and parameters. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))
- **Operation lifecycle:** Encryption or decryption can be performed in one `doFinal` call, or with `update` calls followed by `doFinal`. The Java 26 API says a completed operation attempts to reset to the most recent initialized state, but a reset depends on mode and algorithm; AEAD algorithms may not reset. If reset did not occur, a further `update` or `doFinal` throws `IllegalStateException`, and `init` reinitializes the object. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))
- **Nonce and authentication:** For GCM, Oracle says not to reuse a key–IV combination for encryption and recommends reinitializing for each encryption with different parameters. For GCM or CCM, supply any AAD before processing ciphertext. An AEAD tag is appended during encryption and verified during decryption; a mismatched tag produces `AEADBadTagException`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))
- **Key provenance:** Oracle documents `KeyGenerator` for generating symmetric keys, including initialization with a key size and a source of randomness. Its Cipher documentation does not prescribe a finding-specific key replacement. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/KeyGenerator.html))

**Remediation limit:** Oracle does not recommend removing reinitialization merely because it follows an operation. Its GCM guidance is instead to reinitialize with an appropriate different IV for each encryption. The sources do not prescribe one universal remediation for this detector finding. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))

### 3. Compatibility and migration

- **Persisted and wire data:** Oracle says decryption must use the same algorithm parameters as encryption. Generated parameters can be retrieved through `getParameters`, or an IV through `getIV`. Its GCM example also requires the same AAD for decryption. For wrapped keys, the recipient additionally needs the wrapped key’s algorithm name and type. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))
- **Format implications:** The API does not define a universal application envelope or wire format for storing a transformation, IV, tag length, AAD, and key identifier. Oracle documents that `SealedObject` carries its encryption parameters, but does not provide a general migration procedure for existing application formats. Whether a usage change preserves a particular format is therefore unresolved. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html))
- **Platform support:** `Cipher` has existed since Java 1.4; `GCMParameterSpec` and `updateAAD` are documented since Java 1.7. Java 8’s mandatory transformation list does **not** include AES/GCM, while Java 26’s list includes `AES/GCM/NoPadding` for 128- and 256-bit keys. Absence from the Java 8 mandatory list does not mean every Java 8 provider lacks it. Provider and release documentation remain relevant; GCM tag-length support can also vary by provider. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/crypto/Cipher.html))

### 4. Exact rule in the supplied `Cipher.crysl` source

The file declares `SPEC javax.crypto.Cipher`. Its `Init` event matches the following explicitly listed parameter forms; these are the matching clauses verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

```text
i1: init(encmode, certificate);
i2: init(encmode, certificate, random);
i3: init(encmode, key);
i4: init(encmode, key, paramSpec);
i5: init(encmode, key, params);
i6: init(encmode, key, paramSpec, random);
i7: init(encmode, key, params, random);
i8: init(encmode, key, random);
```

The file declares the associated object types, including `int`, `Key`, `Certificate`, `AlgorithmParameterSpec`, `AlgorithmParameters`, and `SecureRandom`. It also models `getInstance`, `updateAAD`, `update`, `doFinal`, and `wrap`, with specific argument forms. Thus, the rule is **not expressed as an unrestricted name-only match**. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

The sequence condition is this verbatim `ORDER` clause: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

```text
Get, Init+, AADUpdate*, WKB+ | (FINWOU | (Update+, DoFinal))+
```

It contains no `Init` after a modeled finalization or wrapping event. The file separately declares transformation, mode, padding, argument-range, and predicate constraints; those are distinct from this sequence condition. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

**Same-name methods:** The rule declares `javax.crypto.Cipher` as its governed API and lists its event forms; a method on an unrelated type does not become a declared Cipher event merely by sharing its name. The file alone does not specify how a particular analyzer resolves receiver types, aliases, or call targets, so it cannot establish what a particular detector implementation actually matched. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl))

### Source limits

The rule URL points to a moving `master` branch. The retrieved file’s SHA-256 was **not independently verified** against the supplied hash, and the detector version, compiled rule artifact, and analysis configuration were not supplied. Consequently, the exact rule artifact and call resolution behind the reported finding remain unresolved.

- CrySL rule: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl
- Oracle Cipher API, Java 26: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html
- Oracle Cipher API, Java 8: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/crypto/Cipher.html
- Oracle JCA reference guide: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html
- Oracle `GCMParameterSpec`: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html
- Oracle `KeyGenerator`: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/KeyGenerator.html
